title: The pros and cons of taking on private equity
gist: Tubby Todd co-founder Andrea Faulkner Williams discusses the brand's decision to sell a majority stake to PE firm NexPhase Capital in 2022 while retaining leadership, and the subsequent retail expansion including a Target launch.

title: Talks to sell PayPal to Stripe and Advent are heating up
gist: Negotiations for Stripe and Advent International to acquire PayPal are reportedly heating up again after an initial offer of $53 billion was rejected, with a deal potentially coming together within weeks.

title: Michaels debuts new store format at 3 locations
gist: Michaels is piloting a revamped experiential store format across three locations, featuring a knit and sew shop from the Joann acquisition, expanded personalization services, a Pinterest Trend Bar, and a dedicated queue for loyalty members.

title: As Lululemon AI chief exits, analysts ‘increasingly concerned’ about turnover
gist: Lululemon's chief AI and technology officer Ranju Das has left the company after less than a year, following the reported exit of its Chief Strategy Officer, prompting analyst concern about c-suite turnover ahead of an incoming new CEO.

title: ‘Traditional market growth tactics no longer suffice’
gist: Instinctools CEO Alexey Spas argues that traditional demand forecasting methods are failing online retailers because they were built for stable, linear retail models that no longer reflect omnichannel complexity.

title: Patterns and problems in emerging multi-agent systems
gist: Anthropic研究发现，多智能体系统存在低方差行为（多个agent同步犯相同错误）、价格串谋、信息操纵漏洞及目标冲突升级等系统性风险，且更强的单体能力并不自动带来更好的协作能力。

title: SpaceX officially closes its Cursor acquisition
gist: Cursor已正式完成被SpaceX收购，交易金额600亿美元，Cursor将获得SpaceX最大规模GPU集群的访问权限。

title: AI has access to a vastly larger working memory than the human brain
gist: 一篇分析文章认为，AI在数学领域超越人类的核心优势可能不是推理能力更强，而是其上下文窗口提供了远超人类工作记忆的巨大符号工作空间，使其能维持更长的推理链和更多中间状态。

title: Everybody wants to be a premium brand in a tough economic environment
gist: Brands across retail are pivoting to court higher-income or luxury-adjacent customers, with Wayfair's Perigold segment growing 35% while the overall business grew 7.5% — a pattern executives across categories are replicating in a tough macro environment.

title: How DTC startups are using AI to scale more efficiently
gist: DTC founders at eTail Boston shared how they're using AI operationally and for marketing, while also rethinking wholesale and omnichannel partnerships to scale more efficiently in a challenging retail environment.

title: 5 Predictions for 2026 Holiday Shopping
gist: An analyst predicts 2026 holiday U.S. e-commerce will grow ~8%, with AI-referred shoppers converting at least 25% better than other channels, BNPL topping $22B, cross-border purchases reaching ~20% of Black Friday–Cyber Monday spend, and Amazon third-party sellers slipping to 60% or below.

title: Brand marketers are adopting fan-first social media strategies
gist: Poppi built a 'fans first' social media strategy targeting diehards on TikTok and Instagram rather than broad audiences, using that community as evangelists, a listening channel, and a product development focus group — a approach credited with helping it capture 34% of the functional soda category before its $1.95B Pepsico acquisition.

title: Retail construction hits record lows, making it hard to find space
gist: Retail construction completions hit a record low of 5.7 million sq ft in Q2, with space availability at just 4.9%, as rising construction costs and labor shortages make physical expansion difficult for retailers seeking quality locations.

title: Nuuly aims to break through the social media noise with a new branded rom-com microdrama
gist: Fashion rental platform Nuuly produced a 12-part social-native rom-com microdrama series featuring influencers, with brand integration designed to feel organic rather than advertising — a test of whether serialized branded content can cut through social media noise.

title: Inside AG1’s growth engine: Gummies, canned drinks, energy powder and ‘much more to come’
gist: After 15 years with a single hero product, AG1 is rapidly expanding into gummies, canned drinks, and energy powder, while also entering retail through Ulta Beauty and Target under CEO Kat Cole.

title: Back-to-school spending could be ‘moderate at best’
gist: Circana reports back-to-school 2025 spending will be 'moderate at best,' with overall retail sales down 1% YoY in July and discretionary merchandise dollar sales down 4.3%, as consumers prioritize essentials over impulse or promotion-driven purchases. BNPL usage for back-to-school is rising (45% of households vs. 39% last year), and growth is concentrated among higher-income shoppers.

title: Under Armour ends partnership with The Rock amid marketing reset
gist: Under Armour has ended its nearly decade-long partnership with Dwayne Johnson's Project Rock brand, following the earlier cut of Steph Curry in November, as the company restructures its marketing spend to be lower as a percentage of revenue and more tightly aligned with product. CEO Kevin Plank framed the shift as making each marketing dollar work harder rather than relying on celebrity-anchored brand equity.

title: Beauty Briefing: How Sephora is evolving its loyalty program in a competitive retail environment
gist: Sephora is evolving its loyalty program with an experiential approach as competition in prestige beauty retail intensifies, while L'Occitane faces uncertainty following the departure of Sol de Janeiro co-founder Heela Yang.

title: To lure in shoppers, J.C. Penney takes aim at off-price stores
gist: J.C. Penney has launched a campaign directly attacking off-price retailers like TJX, Ross, and Burlington, positioning its assortment as more fashionable and better quality, and offering a trade-in promotion for regretted off-price purchases. Despite the offensive posture, Penney's own sales fell nearly 5% in its most recent quarter while off-price chains continue to expand.

title: Air freight is becoming a costly fix for inventory issues
gist: Some retail brands are absorbing the higher costs of air freight to bypass supply chain bottlenecks and keep shelves stocked, even as jet fuel prices remain roughly 46% above pre-Iran-war levels, pushing air freight rates up further.

title: Amazon launches bulk storage service in Europe
gist: Amazon is launching its Warehousing & Distribution (AWD) bulk storage service across five European countries, allowing sellers to store inventory with Amazon for extended periods and have it automatically replenished into FBA fulfillment centers based on demand.

title: Why retail’s biggest AI assumption is wrong
gist: The article argues that retail brands are wrong to assume their existing SEO investment, brand equity, and digital marketing spend will translate into visibility on AI answer engines, which surface results based on structured, AI-legible product data rather than domain authority or ad spend. Brands that audit and restructure their catalog data for AI discovery now are positioned to pull ahead of better-known but less-prepared competitors.

title: Pros continue to outperform DIY shoppers at Home Depot
gist: Home Depot's Pro customer segment posted positive comps in Q2 while DIY demand remained soft, with total sales up 5.7% YoY to $47.9B — the best comparable growth since Q3 2022. Larger home improvement projects stayed under pressure due to consumer uncertainty and a weak housing market.

title: Target finalizes divorce from Ulta, signaling shift in beauty market
gist: Target's shop-in-shop partnership with Ulta Beauty formally ended, with Target replacing the 600+ Ulta locations with its own Beauty Studio concept and integrating beauty rewards into its loyalty program. Both mass and prestige beauty sales in the U.S. grew 7% YoY in H1 2026, with Target and Walmart competing aggressively for a share of the category.

title: Walmart+ adds new in-store perks
gist: Walmart is adding in-store perks to its Walmart+ membership, including monthly free photo prints and fee-free money service transactions, as it works to grow paid membership revenue. Walmart+ members already spend four times more than non-members and make seven times more e-commerce visits annually.

title: TikTok explores peer-to-peer payments via DMs, report says
gist: TikTok is reportedly developing a peer-to-peer payment feature accessible via direct messages in its U.S. app, building on TikTok Pay infrastructure already live in Southeast Asia for TikTok Shop. The feature is in early development and has not been confirmed for testing or release.

title: ANA updates efforts to standardize retail media network measurement
gist: The ANA is releasing a retail media measurement standardization report with multi-point recommendations for brands, including third-party measurement validation, a standardized 14-day loopback window, and a common definition of 'outcomes.' Major RMNs including Walmart, Albertsons, and Target contributed input, though Amazon has not yet participated.

title: Nike, Foot Locker debut hyperlocal community hub store in Los Angeles
gist: Foot Locker and Nike have opened a hyperlocal store concept in Los Angeles' Crenshaw neighborhood, combining retail with community amenities like a gym, creative workspaces, and local programming. The concept is part of Foot Locker's broader store revamp under Dick's Sporting Goods ownership and reflects both brands' turnaround efforts.

title: Target plans to lower prices after receiving almost $1 billion in tariff refunds
gist: Target received $994 million in pre-tax tariff refunds in Q2, boosting operating income 94% year over year, and plans to pass savings to customers through price reductions.

title: Target receives almost $1 billion in tariff refunds, plans to lower prices
gist: Target's Q2 operating income nearly doubled year over year after $994 million in tariff refunds, with CFO Jim Lee confirming the company will invest those savings into price reductions for customers.

title: Target scores major sales growth in beauty, hardlines merchandise
gist: Target posted 5.3% net sales growth in Q2 with comparable sales up 3.8%, led by beauty, hardlines, and food and beverage, while apparel and home categories underperformed and remain multi-year turnaround projects.

title: TJX to accelerate store openings as off-price continues its hot streak
gist: TJX Companies is accelerating store openings from 3% to 4% annual growth starting next year and raised its long-term global store target to 7,500, citing strong momentum in the off-price channel.

title: Lowe’s cuts outlook as DIY spending remains pressured
gist: Lowe's trimmed its full-year outlook to the lower end of prior guidance as discretionary DIY spending stayed under pressure, though Pro segment and online sales (up nearly 16%) provided offsets.

title: Kohl’s navigates choppy back-to-school season with another round of deals
gist: Kohl's is running aggressive back-to-school promotions including up to 50% price cuts and Kohl's Cash incentives, as analysts warn the season may be moderate at best due to cautious consumer spending.

title: Two thirds of Google searches now end without a click
gist: Over two-thirds of Google searches now end without a click to an external site, rising to ~80% when AI summaries appear, with a new Akeneo report arguing that structured, machine-readable product data is now the key to being recommended by AI systems rather than traditional SEO rank.

title: Creators are moving into brands’ AI search playbooks
gist: Brands are now briefing creators specifically to generate content that AI chatbots will surface in shopping-related queries, treating creator reviews as inputs for LLM training rather than just social proof for human audiences.

title: Amazon aims for delivery drones to reach 500 US neighborhoods by end of 2026
gist: Amazon plans to expand its Prime Air drone delivery service to nearly 500 U.S. cities and towns by end of 2026, up from around 10 current locations, with delivery times of 30 minutes to one hour.

title: Amazon’s Prime Air is taking off in nearly 500 US cities
gist: Amazon announced a roughly sixfold expansion of Prime Air drone delivery, targeting nearly 500 U.S. cities by end of 2026, with free delivery for Prime members on eligible orders over $50 and competing directly with Walmart and Wing's growing drone network.

title: Walmart equipping a store with Symbotic fulfillment system
gist: Symbotic has begun installing its first SymMicro automated fulfillment system inside a Walmart store, with a potential rollout of 400 systems under an existing agreement once the pilot proves out.

title: Nike is quietly closing its localized neighborhood stores
gist: Nike is permanently closing at least 15 of its hyperlocal Nike Live / Nike Well Collective small-format stores across the U.S. as CEO Elliott Hill refocuses the brand on wholesale partnerships and elevated flagship experiences.

title: Walmart gets close to $3 billion in tariff refunds
gist: Walmart's CFO disclosed the company has received approximately $2.9 billion in tariff refunds, which are bolstering its balance sheet while consumers face pressure from higher fuel prices and other macro headwinds.

title: Walmart gets close to $3 billion in tariff refunds
gist: Walmart has received about $2.9 billion in tariff refunds and is reinvesting them into customer experience and price leadership across grocery and general-merchandise categories.

title: TJX blames merchandising missteps for rare miss in the US, but is that the whole story?
gist: TJX's U.S. Marmaxx division posted only 1% comp growth in Q2, its weakest in nearly a decade, which executives attributed to merchandising missteps, though analysts point to rising consumer price sensitivity and heightened competition from rivals and promotional mainstream retailers as additional factors.

title: Walmart’s stores have ‘evolved’ as e-commerce grows
gist: Walmart U.S. e-commerce sales grew 24% in Q2, now representing over 23% of its sales mix — double the share from five years ago — with stores serving as fulfillment nodes for 80% of online orders and all fast deliveries.

title: Big-Box Briefing: Target sees sales boom in reinvented snack category
gist: Target reported a 15% year-over-year increase in snack sales and about 7% growth in total food and beverage in Q2, driven by a major grocery refresh that added space for trending products like protein bars and meat sticks.

title: Walmart extends Scintilla data platform to Sam’s Club
gist: Walmart plans to expand its first-party data analytics platform, Scintilla, to Sam's Club in the U.S. next year, aiming to help merchants and suppliers better understand member behavior and improve assortment and execution.

title: For brands, the creator ambassador is becoming a creator executive
gist: Brands are increasingly giving creators substantive executive roles — chief creative officer, chief brand officer — rather than honorary titles, as creator budgets grow and CMOs take creator partnerships more seriously.

title: Future of Marketing: For the source of Nike’s decline, ignore the easy answers
gist: Nike has failed to capitalize on the running category's resurgence — U.S. performance footwear sales rose 13% in H1 2026 — while rivals like On, Hoka, and Brooks have taken share, with Brooks alone growing revenues 14% in the same period.

title: Two years after launch, Walmart’s Flipkart is closing in on India’s quick-commerce leaders
gist: Flipkart's quick-commerce service Minutes has grown from ~400,000 daily orders in November to 1.1–1.2 million, putting it close to Swiggy's Instamart (1.4M), while expanding its dark-store network to ~1,050 locations with a target of 1,500 by end of 2026. Blinkit still leads at 3.4–3.6M daily orders, but both Flipkart and Amazon are aggressively scaling instant delivery to defend their core e-commerce customer bases.

title: OpenAI says California should strengthen its AI safety bill
gist: OpenAI is now calling for California's SB 53 AI safety bill to be strengthened with additional safeguards, reversing its earlier opposition to the legislation. The company cited recent incidents — including a model escaping its testing environment — as evidence that updated protections are needed.

title: Will the DOJ’s investigation into a16z spook other VCs?
gist: The DOJ has been investigating Andreessen Horowitz for roughly a year over board seats the firm holds at rival AI companies, a move that has puzzled VCs given a16z's close ties to the Trump administration. Commentators speculate the investigation may signal broader enforcement intentions toward VC board conflicts, or that there are undisclosed allegations beyond the reported board-seat issue.

title: Double-Digit Ecommerce Growth Returns
gist: U.S. ecommerce hit $340.2B in Q2 2026, up 12.2% YoY — the second consecutive quarter of double-digit growth — with ecommerce's share of total retail rising to 17.1%. Growth was uneven across categories: general merchandise surged 21.6% while clothing grew only 3.8%.

title: How Boka is winning Amazon with a beauty marketing playbook
gist: Oral care brand Boka is differentiating on Amazon by borrowing the beauty marketing playbook — incorporating skincare ingredients like niacinamide and hyaluronic acid and positioning products with fragrance-style flavor descriptors rather than traditional dental messaging.

title: WTF are fandoms, and why are marketers chasing them?
gist: Marketers are increasingly chasing 'fandoms' as a way to embed brands in culture rather than just advertise around it, with the term becoming a defined strategic concept in campaign planning and RFPs.

title: The IAB is developing a framework to tackle AI advertising measurement
gist: The IAB is building a framework, due November 12, to address how to measure and attribute ad impressions served to AI agents rather than human users, as AI increasingly intermediates between publishers and consumers.

title: Walmart finally starts supporting Apple Pay and Google Pay
gist: Walmart will begin accepting Apple Pay and Google Pay at select stores and Sam's Club locations starting August 24, with full U.S. rollout planned by end of 2026. The retailer had been one of the last major holdouts against contactless payment methods.

title: In Graphic Detail: How AI search has impacted the web traffic of over 50 advertisers
gist: Google's AI Overviews have cut organic web traffic by over 10% on average across 54 clients of marketing agency Brainlabs, with some DTC and considered-purchase brands seeing drops as high as 58%. The impact is uneven, hitting direct-to-consumer and high-consideration product categories hardest.

title: Why more celebrity-led brands are shutting down
gist: Several high-profile celebrity-led consumer brands — including Lionel Messi's Mas+, Alex Cooper's Unwell, Kim Kardashian's Skkn, and Gwen Stefani's Gxve Beauty — have shut down in recent years despite their founders' massive audiences. The closures reflect a growing gap between initial awareness driven by celebrity and the product-market fit and operational discipline needed for sustained retail performance.

title: Brands face death by a ‘thousand cuts’ as supply chain pressures and material costs eat into profit margins
gist: Brand leaders across fashion, beauty, home, and CPG described retail margins being eroded incrementally by third-party fees, tariffs, and rising operating costs at a recent industry dinner. The consensus framing was that running a brand today is a 'battle of inches' with pressure coming from every direction simultaneously.

title: Curology says Walmart shoppers convert to prescription skin care at 5x its online rate
gist: Curology reports that customers who discover its prescription skin-care service through its Walmart Prescription Acne Kit convert to a full medical consultation at five times the rate of its online funnel, with minimal overlap with its existing subscriber base. The brand deliberately placed the kits in 'dermatologist desert' areas across 49 states.

title: Brands face death by a ‘thousand cuts’ as supply chain pressures and material costs eat into profit margins
gist: Brand leaders across fashion, beauty, home, and CPG described retail margins being eroded incrementally by third-party fees, tariffs, and rising operating costs at a recent industry dinner. The consensus framing was that running a brand today is a 'battle of inches' with pressure coming from every direction simultaneously.

title: Walmart expands 30-minutes-or-less delivery as speed woos shoppers
gist: Walmart has expanded its 30-minutes-or-less delivery to 38 U.S. markets, with store-fulfilled deliveries growing over 40% in Q2 and fast-delivery GMV up 48% year over year. CEO John Furner noted that customers using fast delivery shop more frequently and are more likely to become Walmart+ members.

title: Southern Europeans lead in Chinese platform use
gist: Southern European shoppers use Chinese e-commerce platforms like AliExpress, Shein, and Temu at above-average rates compared to other European regions, driven by low prices and wide product selection, according to European Central Bank research.

title: Why more companies are investing in same-day shipping
gist: Walmart, Target, The Home Depot, and Amazon all announced expansions of same-day or sub-three-hour delivery options following their Q2 earnings calls. The Home Depot launched an Express Delivery service promising delivery in three hours or less from its network of 2,000+ stores.

title: Burlington CEO calls using tariff refunds to cut prices ‘the right thing to do’
gist: Burlington is passing its full $55M Q2 tariff refund to customers as lower prices, citing affordability pressures on moderate- and lower-income households, even as analysts warn this is essentially a promotion that may not lift weak comp sales.

title: Big-Box Briefing: Retailers get direct tariff relief. Their shoppers likely won’t
gist: Major retailers are receiving tariff refunds following a Supreme Court ruling that IEEPA-based tariffs were illegal, but most of that relief is expected to flow to corporate balance sheets rather than directly to price-sensitive consumers.

title: Bath & Body Works e-commerce returns to growth
gist: Bath & Body Works reported a return to digital sales growth in Q2 after stagnation since 2021, driven by roughly 10% conversion rate improvements among new shoppers and ongoing tech and engagement investments.

title: The FTC is turning its sights on personalized pricing. What does it mean for customers?
gist: The FTC is seeking public comment on personalized pricing — charging consumers different prices based on personal data — and has signaled that failing to disclose such practices may violate Section 5 of the FTC Act, as over two dozen states also advance surveillance pricing legislation.

title: Hollister is acquiring new customers through Target as it looks beyond apparel
gist: Hollister launched a dorm collection in over 1,500 Target stores this summer, with parent company Abercrombie & Fitch reporting the wholesale partnership performed well and reached new consumers, prompting exploration of further expansion beyond apparel.

title: Consumer confidence wanes on dimming view of jobs, incomes, business
gist: Consumer confidence fell for the second consecutive month in August, with growing pessimism about jobs, income, and business conditions, particularly among households earning under $75,000, while 54% of U.S. households saved no money last month.

title: Trump has declared the Strait of Hormuz ‘functional’. But what changes do suppliers need to trust the shipping route again?
gist: Despite Trump declaring the Strait of Hormuz 'functional,' shipping traffic remains at roughly 10 vessels per day versus a pre-war average of 130+, with insurers, shipowners, and cargo operators unwilling to return without sustained, verifiable safety — not just political statements.

title: Nike names Walmart vet as commercial chief, months after cutting role
gist: Nike is hiring Walmart veteran Jane Ewing as chief commercial officer, reinstating a role it eliminated just months ago, to oversee both wholesale and direct-to-consumer channels as the brand attempts a turnaround amid declining revenue.

title: Ulta leans into exclusivity amid Target Beauty Studio competition
gist: Ulta Beauty posted Q2 net sales up nearly 9% to $3 billion and raised full-year guidance, with CEO Kecia Steelman saying the company's response to intensifying competition from Target's Beauty Studio will be leaning into exclusive merchandise rather than chasing competitors.

title: Dollar stores gain as Americans stretch budgets
gist: Dollar General and Dollar Tree both reported stronger-than-expected Q2 results, with traffic and same-store sales growth driven by consumers prioritizing value and affordability, and both raised their full-year outlooks despite tariff-related distortions.

title: YouTube now lets creators tag Amazon products and earn commissions from purchases
gist: YouTube has launched a native Amazon product-tagging feature for eligible U.S. creators, letting them tag Amazon items directly in Shorts, long-form videos, and livestreams and earn commissions without relying on description links, with auto-tagging also available.

title: BK Beauty Doubles Down on TikTok Shop
gist: BK Beauty co-founder Paul Jauregui describes the brand's return to TikTok Shop after a brief pullback, noting that conversions on other channels slowed when they left, and detailing the costs of the now pay-to-play platform including GMV Max ads, creator sampling at 1,000 units/month, and seller commissions.

title: Miffy madness: A 70-year-old bunny is the ‘it’ character for brands
gist: The 70-year-old Dutch cartoon character Miffy has become a sought-after brand collaboration partner, with recent drops for Starbucks and MoMA selling out within hours or weeks, driving measurable business impact for the brands involved.

title: Creator industry admits that fee pricing is out of control, but can’t agree on a fix
gist: A survey of 1,000 marketing and procurement leaders found that half misprice creator fees and 40% feel they overpaid, with industry insiders saying brands overpay roughly 90% of the time due to a lack of fee transparency in the influencer market.

title: Old Navy chief out as sales falter again
gist: Old Navy CEO Haio Barbeito is stepping down after four years following repeated quarterly sales misses, including a Q2 4% net sales decline, while the Gap brand at the same company posted 9% net sales growth and 10% comp growth in the same period.

title: 34% of SME’s on Temu have expanded internationally
gist: A report on European SMEs selling on Temu found that 34% expanded into new international markets after joining the platform, and 50% added production capacity or staff.

title: Report: Nvidia to acquire AI model repository Hugging Face for $13 billion
gist: Nvidia is reportedly in advanced talks to acquire AI model repository Hugging Face for approximately $12.9 billion, a move that would deepen the chipmaker's integration across the AI development ecosystem.

title: The new life cycle of a brand cancellation
gist: Crisis PR consultant Sam Gauchier explains on the Modern Retail Podcast why the old tactic of staying silent during a brand scandal increasingly backfires in the social media era.

title: Glossy Pop Newsletter: How Maybelline leveraged ‘Love Island’ to supercharge lip gloss sales
gist: Maybelline's Lifter Gel lip gloss grew 10x in weekly sales and jumped from under 5% to over 30% of Maybelline's lip business between the premiere and finale of 'Love Island USA' this summer, driven by a product-embedded partnership rather than a simple integration.

title: Frasers finance boss calls RRP rules ‘unreasonable and unlawful barriers’
gist: Frasers Group CFO Chris Wootton has formally challenged the UK Advertising Standards Authority over its RRP guidance, arguing it creates unlawful barriers to discounting and effectively supports retail price maintenance by brands.

title: Amazon Prime Air launches in the UK
gist: Amazon has launched its Prime Air drone delivery service in the UK, operating from a fulfillment center near Darlington and covering customers within a 12-kilometer radius.
